verification.notes: Preferred level is complete: revised Section 7.7 states an unconditional prohibition on Customer-payable liquidated damages and penalties, and the offending 15%-of-annual-Fees-per-week formula is removed rather than merely capped, so no residual mechanic remains. Fallback elements are satisfied vacuously because no Customer-payable liquidated amount or early-termination fee survives anywhere in the operative text; the three-month cap is reserved to the comment as a negotiating position only, which is appropriate and does not affect completeness. Minimality holds: the edit is confined to Section 7.7, the only clause imposing a Customer-payable liquidated amount. Sections 7.3 (disputed amounts, no interest on disputed sums), 9.4 and 27 are untouched, and no survival tail, damages category, procedure or unrelated boilerplate is added. The words "or any Order Form" are within the target scope, closing the obvious circumvention route rather than importing an outside requirement. Intent is preserved: no defined term is orphaned and no cross-reference dangles — Section 7.7 was self-contained, and the replacement sentence sits consistently with the retained payment mechanics. Vendor's ordinary remedies for non-payment (suspension/termination for material breach, collection of unpaid Fees) are unaffected because only the liquidated-damages formula was excised. No double-flagging: this term is not also captured under T4C or RENEWAL, since termination without cause carries only accrued Fees and Section 27 is expressly without penalty. Severity is raised because the original clause was walk-away territory — a weekly-compounding 15% of annual Fees triggered by a minor payment delay can exceed the remaining contract value — so the finding should be pressed as non-negotiable rather than merely a high-priority ask.

mappings.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
mappings.quote: 8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent.

quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand.
rationale: Section 8.2 provides automatic renewals of successive twelve-month periods (no multi-year renewal), a Customer non-renewal notice window of only thirty days (within the preferred 30-day ceiling and well inside the fallback 60 days), and an express Vendor reminder obligation at least sixty days before renewal, reinforced by an extension of Customer's opt-out deadline if the reminder is not sent. Section 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of US CPI-U over the preceding twelve months and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. This meets every preferred atomic element, so the conditional automatic-renewal path applies and mutual written agreement is not required. No redline needed.

mappings.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
mappings.quote: Within thirty days after Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format

quote: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form.
rationale: Section 11 satisfies the preferred position on its material terms and comfortably clears the fallback: assistance is triggered by expiry or termination for any reason (not conditioned on a pre-expiry request or on Customer being non-breaching), runs up to six months (well beyond the 90-day fallback), Customer Data is returned within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with metadata, and an authorized officer certifies deletion in writing after Customer confirms successful return. Two variances are in our favour and are noted rather than flagged: assistance is priced at the rates in the expiring Order Form rather than Vendor's then-current rates (rate protection for us), and the thirty-day return clock runs from our request rather than from termination, with Vendor expressly barred from withholding Customer Data over a fee dispute. Section 15 contains no conflicting immediate-deletion mechanic, and Section 16.3 confirms Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

quote: 19.1 Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.
rationale: Section 19 meets the preferred position and comfortably clears the fallback. Services (defined in § 1.8 to include the hosted software) are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner and to conform materially to their documentation with no time limit (19.1), Deliverables conform for ninety days after delivery or acceptance and the hosted Services conform throughout the subscription term (19.2), and Vendor warrants compliance with Applicable Law and absence of malicious code (19.3). Remedies include re-performance, repair or replacement plus a refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure (19.4), and the disclaimer in 19.5 expressly does not limit any express warranty, so it does not swallow the warranty. Minor points noted but not redlined: the malicious-code warranty is limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", the refund is available only after failed cure, and "Hosted Services" is used without a separate definition (it reads on the hosted software within the defined Services).

rationale: Section 18 is an operative Vendor insurance covenant that meets every preferred element: CGL of USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, professional E&O of USD 2,000,000, cyber and privacy liability of USD 5,000,000 (unconditional, and Vendor does host and process Customer Data), workers' compensation as required by law, and certificates of insurance on request under Section 18.2. Extras in our favour (employer's liability, one-year tail, primary-cover and non-limitation language) are additive and do not warrant comment. Sits at the preferred position, so no redline.
